rationale: Direct swap of plain polyethylene for borated polyethylene in the known all-PASS 105cm PE + 5cm Pb prior design. Boron-10 capture emits far fewer/lower-energy gammas than hydrogen capture, so this should not raise (and may lower) the photon dose versus the prior, while removal cross-section (0.110/cm, same as plain PE) preserves neutron attenuation. Screening to compare nominal R1 and mass against the prior baseline.

Single-layer borated polyethylene at the thickness of the prior's best pure-PE case (120cm PE alone passed R1/R2 but failed R3-photon badly at 10.5-10.9 uSv/h). Testing whether boron's suppressed capture-gamma yield could let a lead-free design work, which would remove ~570 kg/m2 of lead mass. Screen only checks R1/mass here; photon behavior cannot be confirmed without an evaluate, which I have zero budget for this round.

If boron reduces capture-gamma production, a thinner lead cap (3cm instead of 5cm) may suffice for R3-photon while keeping neutron shielding identical to the all-PASS 105cm-PE+5cm-Pb prior. Would save ~23 kg/m2 of lead mass if it holds up under full transport, which I cannot check this round (0 evaluate budget).

Push moderator thickness down 5cm from the all-PASS prior baseline (mirroring the prior's own 100cm-PE+5Pb attempt, which failed R2-neutron with a [6.57,10] uSv/h band against the 7 limit). Borated PE's identical removal cross-section to plain PE means this is expected to show similar or slightly worse R1/neutron margin; screening to see the nominal number and mass trade-off for the record, not because I expect it to be safe.
